memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Abram lived in the land of Canaan, while Lot lived among the cities of the plain and pitched his tents near Sodom. Now the people of Sodom were wicked and were sinning greatly against the Lord. - Gen 13:12-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is one of the saddest sentences in Genesis: Lot "pitched his tents near Sodom." Not in Sodom - not yet. Just near it. He kept his distance while drifting steadily closer. And Scripture tells us plainly what Sodom was: a place where people "were wicked and were sinning greatly against the Lord."

Lot did not choose Sodom's sin. He chose its scenery. But you cannot pitch your tent near something without being pulled toward it. Read on in Genesis and you will find Lot living in Sodom, then sitting in its gate as a leader, then losing nearly everything when judgement falls. The drift that began with a glance ended in disaster.

This is how compromise almost always works. Nobody decides to ruin their life. They simply move a little closer, and then a little closer, telling themselves they are still outside. But proximity shapes us. What we camp beside eventually gets inside us.

Scripture is realistic about this: "Do not be misled: 'Bad company corrupts good character'" (1 Cor 15:33). Notice too that Peter later calls Lot "righteous" and "distressed" by what surrounded him (2 Pet 2:7-8) - he was a believer, tormented but still there. It is possible to be God's and still be slowly destroyed by where you have pitched your tent. Ask honestly: what am I camping beside?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What are you living "near" that you would never choose directly?
- Where has drift moved you closer to compromise than you realise?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, show me where I have pitched my tent too close to what harms me. Give me courage to move, and keep me from the slow drift that ends far from You.
Amen.
